title: Opening a store already at target version is a silent no-op
asA: operator whose routine boots must not emit spurious migrated events
iWant: the migration runner to apply no work and emit no migrated event when the on-disk version already equals the build's max
soThat: a migrated event in the log means real schema evolution and my post-migration bookkeeping does not fire on every boot

acceptanceCriteria.description: Opening a store whose bookkeeping table records the same schema version the build's max known migration version equals results in a migration run whose applied-versions array is empty and no changes to the store artifact.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a store artifact whose highest bookkeeping row records version N and a build whose max known migration version is N
acceptanceCriteria.when: the boot sequence invokes the open entry point
acceptanceCriteria.then: the migration run's applied-versions array is empty, no new bookkeeping row has been written, and a byte-for-byte comparison of the store artifact before and after the open shows no schema-affecting change

acceptanceCriteria.description: On the no-op open path, the opened event fires but the migrated event does NOT fire; the sink receives one opened record and zero migrated records.
acceptanceCriteria.given: the no-op open in AC-5111-1 with an event sink attached
acceptanceCriteria.when: the sink is inspected after the open entry point returns
acceptanceCriteria.then: the sink has received exactly one opened record and zero migrated records for this open

acceptanceCriteria.description: No-op boot: the artefact bytes on disk are unchanged. Given the store artefact on disk at the target schema version and a byte-hash captured before boot, when the process boots and closes without any consumer write, then the byte-hash after boot equals the byte-hash before boot; a mutation SIMULATE_PHANTOM_WRITE=true triggers a metadata write during the no-op boot and the byte-hash assertion FAILS.
acceptanceCriteria.given: store artefact at target version; byte-hash captured before boot
acceptanceCriteria.when: process boots and closes without consumer writes
acceptanceCriteria.then: byte-hash after boot equals byte-hash before boot; the phantom-write mutation FAILS
